cards.text: Right before this, Joel the prophet calls the priests to cry out, 'Spare Your people, O LORD.' Lean in, friend, because here comes the answer. The LORD becomes jealous for His land.

cards.question: The LORD is jealous for His land. What does He do for His people?

cards.text: Then the LORD answers His people, and friend, there's no hold music and no 'please stay on the line.' He ANSWERS.

cards.question: God tells His people what He'll send them, so they'll be satisfied. What is it?

answers.text: Grain and new wine and oil

cards.question: Joel had the priests pray that God's people wouldn't become a reproach among the nations. Now God says He will never again make them one.

cards.text: Next, God talks about the northern army, and He is NOT asking it nicely to leave. He says He'll drive it away to a barren and desolate land.

cards.question: God splits up the northern army. Its front ranks go into the Eastern Sea, and its rear guard into the ___ Sea.

cards.text: Then its stench rises, and its foul odor goes up. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer under takeout menus nobody had touched in forever, and I STILL don't want a whiff of that.
Then the words turn to the land itself: 'Do not be afraid, O land.' The DIRT is getting a pep talk, friend, and it's a better one than I ever got in that drawer.

cards.question: The land is told not to be afraid, but to rejoice and be glad. Why?

answers.text: Because the LORD has done great things
Because the people have done great things
Because the enemy has begged for peace

cards.text: Now the beasts of the field get the same word: do not be afraid. Even the animals are being told to relax, and I bet some of those cows really needed to hear it.

cards.question: The beasts of the field don't need to fear, because the open pastures have turned ___.
In this promise, the trees bear their fruit, but the fig tree and the vine still hold back their best.

cards.text: First the land, then the animals, and now God's people, the children of Zion, are told to be glad and rejoice in the LORD their God. Friend, this pep talk has a GUEST LIST.

cards.question: Zion's children have a reason to be glad. What has the LORD given them, as before?

answers.text: A new king on the throne

cards.question: With the rains back, the threshing floors will be ___ of grain, and the vats will ___ with new wine and oil.

cards.text: Then God speaks again. He looks back at the years eaten by locusts.

cards.question: God says He will ___ His people for the years eaten by locusts.

cards.text: REPAY the years, friend! Even the expired coupon from my old drawer, the one that never stopped believing in itself, never promised THAT.

cards.question: God names four kinds of locusts: swarming, young, destroying and devouring. What does He call them?

answers.text: My great army that I sent
The plague the north wind carried

cards.text: God says they'll have plenty to eat until they're satisfied, and they'll praise the name of the LORD their God, who has worked wonders for them. Not scrape-the-bottom-of-the-bowl plenty, friend. PLENTY plenty.

cards.question: God says His people will be put to shame one more time before things get better.

cards.text: And here's the big finish. God says all of this leads to something His people will know.

cards.question: When God does all this, what will His people know?

answers.text: That God is present in Israel
That the harvest will last forever
That the locusts will never return

cards.question: God tells His people He is the LORD their God, but there are other gods like Him.

findings.problem: The opening card gives the priests' prayer but never says what has been happening: the land has been stripped and the people are asking God to spare them. Locusts don't come up until stop 2 card 4. Without that context, God's promise of grain, new wine and oil (stop 1 card 4) and the green pastures (card 12) are harder to reason out, and the restoration has nothing to answer.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The statement is true only because of two verses: the priests' prayer about a reproach (Joel 2:17) and God's promise (Joel 2:19). The card cites only Joel 2:19, and the reproach part of 2:17 was never told on card 1.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: This story card only reacts to the repay promise the baker just answered on card 5. It tells no new part of the passage, so it works as a recap that carries a joke instead of moving the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'My great army that I sent', is in God's first-person voice. The wrong answers are in third person, so the right one stands out. 'The enemy that came uninvited' is also close to the right answer, since the locusts were an army sent against the people, and a baker could argue for it.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences. It also carries two beats (plenty to eat, and praising God) plus the joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
